title: Traffic sweep and soft-variant migration: regional fallback & deprecation safeguard
creator: Ethan Chen
description:
Goal: implement a safe, observable policy layer that handles traffic sweep and soft migration for pinned model versions across regions and model variants while surfacing deprecation signals to customers.

Context: customers can pin to a specific model revision. When that revision is deprecated, evicted, or unavailable in a region we must route traffic to compatible alternatives without surprising latency/cost regressions or quality drops. Existing work covers basic failover; this ticket defines the traffic-sweep strategy (gradual traffic migration + warmup), compatibility fences, telemetry hooks, and the controlled deprecation path for pinned versions.

Non-goals: automated model compatibility changes that alter outputs; this ticket focuses on routing, gating, and observability rather than model transformation or acceptance testing of alternative model outputs.
acceptance_criteria: A policy API exists to declare fallback horizons for a pinned version (regional priority list, allowed variants, max latency uplift).
Traffic-sweep controller can route X% of traffic to fallback variant and incrementally ramp to 100% with configurable step and cooldown.
KV-cache warmup and slice-based batching hooks ensure fallbacks do not cause a cold-start spike exceeding defined latency SLOs.
Telemetry: per-pin telemetry (latency, cost-per-token, failure-rate, eval-quality-probe results) is emitted to the console and runtime dashboards during the sweep.

Deprecation workflow: when a pin enters deprecation, customers receive a notification with suggested compatible variants; automatic soft-migration starts only after a TTL has passed and if the customer has not responded.
Canary rollback: controller supports automatic rollback to previous variant if regression signals exceed thresholds (error-rate, customer-eval-failures).
Unit and integration tests cover routing decisions for region down, variant mismatch, and phased sweep behavior.
work_items: Design fallback policy schema and API (runtime + control plane)
Implement traffic-sweep controller with ramp scheduler and cooldown enforcement
Add warmup hooks: KV-cache prefill and controlled batch sizing
Integrate telemetry events and console visualization (per-pin timeline)
Deprecation UX: notification templates and TTL policy
QA: run chaos scenarios (region outage, memory pressure, coldpool replenishment)
notes: Initial spike analysis showed naive failover increases p99 by ~120ms due to cold KV caches; warmup required.
We should reuse the existing rollout library but extend it to support per-pin compatibility fences and variant acceptance criteria.
Conservative defaults: ramp=10% steps, cooldown=10 minutes, max-allowed-latency-uplift=20%
Dependency on runtime kernel selection change to tag warmup traffic at lower priority (ENG-50021 follow-up).
